en: Points of Controversy The Great Fifty-Section The Sixteenth Chapter
The Discussion on Whether Matter is Wholesome or Unwholesome.
Is matter wholesome? Yes.
"It has an object; it has turning toward it... aspiration"?
One should not say so...
Is it not the case that it has no object, and that there is no turning toward it... nor aspiration?
“Yes.
“If it is without an object, then there is for it no turning toward [the object], nor … [down to] … aspiration. Therefore, indeed, you should not say:
‘Form is wholesome.’”
Non-greed is wholesome and has an object; does it have turning toward [the object], and so on, up to aspiration?
Yes. Is material form wholesome and has an object; does it have turning toward [the object], and so on, up to aspiration? No.
It should not be said thus ... [as before] ...
non-hatred is wholesome ... [as before] ...
non-delusion is wholesome ... [as before].
Faith … energy … mindfulness …
“Is concentration … pe … wisdom wholesome and with an object? Is there, by means of it, turning toward … pe … aspiration?
“Yes.”
Is material form wholesome and with an object, and does it possess turning toward [the object], and so forth, up to aspiration?
One should not say so...
Is material form wholesome and without an object, and does it lack turning toward [the object], and so forth, up to aspiration? One should not say so either...pe... [end of elision].
“Yes,” [you say].
“Then is non-greed wholesome and without an object, and for it there is no turning toward, … [and so on] … no aspiration?
You should not speak thus … [and so on] …
Is wholesome material form (rūpa) without an object (anārammaṇa), and does it lack turning toward [the object], and so forth, up to aspiration (paṇidhi)?
Yes. Is wholesome non-hatred (adosa) likewise? Yes.
“Is wisdom unwholesome and without an object? Is there no turning toward it …pe… nor aspiration?
One should not say so …pe….
“Is material form unwholesome?”
“Yes,” [you say].
“Does it have an object? Is there its turning toward [the object] … down to … its aspiration?
You should not speak thus … [as before] …
But is it not the case that it has no object, and for it there is no turning toward [the object], nor... nor aspiration?
Yes, it is so.
If it has no object, and for it there is no turning toward [the object], nor... nor aspiration, then indeed you should not say: [that it is a state of mind].
“Form is unwholesome,” and so forth...
Greed is unwholesome and has an object; is there its turning toward [the object], and so forth, up to its aspiration?
Yes, there is.
“Is form unwholesome, with an object, and does it have turning toward, [and so on] … up to … aspiration?
One should not say this … [etc.
… there is a fault.
Is delusion … conceit … [and so on] … lack of moral dread unwholesome and with an object? Is there for it turning toward … [and so on] … aspiration?
“Yes,” [you say].
“Is form unwholesome and with an object, and does it have turning toward, and so forth, up to, aspiration?
You should not speak thus … and so on.
Is material form unwholesome and without an object, such that there is for it no turning toward [the object], nor … nor aspiration?
Yes. Is greed unwholesome and without an object, such that there is for it no turning toward [the object], nor … nor aspiration? [Yes.]
It should not be said thus ... [as before] ...
Is it the case that material form is unwholesome and without an object, and that for it there is no turning toward, ... [as before] ... nor aspiration?
Yes, it is.
Is hatred ... delusion ... and so on ...
lack of moral dread unwholesome and without an object; is there no turning toward it ... and so on ... up to no aspiration for it?
It should not be said thus...
[as before] ... Should it not be said that "form is both wholesome and unwholesome"?
“Yes.
“But is it not the case that bodily action and verbal action are both wholesome and unwholesome?
“Yes.”
If bodily action and verbal action are both wholesome and unwholesome, then indeed, it must be said:
"Material form is both wholesome and unwholesome.
The discussion on whether material form is wholesome or unwholesome is concluded.
